title: AI-powered Chatbot for official website of NSO India
purpose: Dissemination / communication: Supporting the presentation, explanation, or communication of statistics (e.g. generating statistical releases, narratives, data visualisations, metadata, or user-facing summaries)
maturity: Production (operational): The AI application is integrated into routine statistical operations and is used on a regular basis to support official statistics
business_need:
The official website of NSO, India (www.mospi.gov.in) is an important public interface and digital face of NSO India, which serves as a comprehensive resource, offering access to various statistical surveys, programs, schemes, and initiatives. It also provides varied and crucial information related to MoSPI to its various stakeholders viz. news, events, publications, and data downloads, providing users with detailed information on macroeconomic aggregates, state domestic products, GDP, and more.
The website hosts a large volume of data and information on various statistical products spread across sections of the website and across multiple formats (text, PDFs, Excel etc.). However, a user needs to know in which relevant section/ product to look into, for accessing relevant information. For example, to know employment/ unemployment rate for any State/UT or sector, the user needs to go to the PLFS reports page, about which he may not be aware. This makes it more difficult for users, especially those not well-versed in statistics, in quickly accessing relevant information, datasets, reports, and statistical documents and interpret required information. This often leads to increased dependency on manual support, delays in information retrieval, and reduced user satisfaction.
description: This chatbot delivers intelligent and contextual responses to user queries, ensuring relevant and accurate information retrieval, leveraging advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Generative AI.
benefits: The AI-powered chatbot has led to improved accessibility by enabling faster and simpler retrieval of datasets, reports, and statistical content without requiring deep navigation.
challenges: The Chatbot required training on data stored in different formats like pdfs, scanned pdfs, etc. Hence, significant effort was needed in preprocessing the documents to make them AI-ready. Since it is a chatbot for the Government, utmost care was needed and proper guardrailing was done to ensure that the chatbot responded only on the information available on the website and does not add any opinion or any information outside the scope of NSO, India website.
governance_measures: Documentation of model and limitations;Risk or ethics assessment;Human-in-the-loop oversight;Data protection / confidentiality procedures
ethics_note: The NSO India website chatbot utilizes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), a framework that ensures high accuracy by pulling information directly from official reports, publications and press releases. To guarantee reliability, the system underwent rigorous testing to ensure it provides factual data without including personal opinions. Additionally, the chatbot is evaluated to ensure its responses are ethical, unbiased, and fair. Every response during evaluation phase is cross-checked against original publications to maintain accountability and ensure information remains consistent with content of the NSO India website.
links: The Chatbot can be accessed at https://www.mospi.gov.in/; the GitHub link may be accessed at https://github.com/nso-india/mospi-llm-chatbot-v1.

models_or_algorithms: Random Forest classifiers (including GPU-accelerated versions), convolutional neural networks for semantic segmentation (U-Net with ResNet backbones), and principal component analysis for dimensionality reduction.

business_need: Highly climate-exposed countries often lack integrated, decision-ready systems that translate climate and disaster risk data into timely action. In Vanuatu, data on cyclones, droughts, floods, and slow-onset climate impacts existed across multiple agencies, but there was no unified system to analyse this information and trigger preparedness, response, or financing decisions. This resulted in delayed assessments, fragmented coordination, and reactive responses that increased losses for vulnerable populations. The initiative addresses this gap by creating a national, AI-enabled loss and damage decision system that links climate risk indicators to causal impact models, operational thresholds, and trigger-based decision processes for anticipatory action, response, and recovery.
description: AI and machine learning are used to analyse satellite imagery and environmental data to generate real-time indicators of climate change and disaster impacts, such as land cover, flooding, soil health, coastal erosion, and temperature trends. These indicators are integrated with census and administrative data through automated analytical pipelines to estimate exposure, damage, resource needs, and financial losses. The outputs feed into a national management information system that supports trigger-based decisions for anticipatory action, emergency response, and recovery financing.
benefits:
- Rapid estimation of disaster impacts and resource needs through automated analytical pipelines. 
- Integration of machine learning outputs, census data, and administrative data into a single national decision platform. 
- Improved timeliness and consistency of impact assessments across sectors. 
- Enhanced coordination across ministries and disaster response clusters through a centralised system. 
- Strengthened local capacity in geospatial analysis, machine learning, and reproducible analytical pipelines. 
- Land classification model achieved approximately 82% accuracy, enabling reliable environmental monitoring.
challenges:
- Fragmented legacy data systems and inconsistent data quality across sectors. 
- Limited technical capacity for machine learning, remote sensing, and open-source analytical tools. 
- Need for extensive data cleaning, harmonisation, and interoperability between systems. 
- Institutional coordination challenges across ministries and stakeholders. 
- Requirement for human-in-the-loop validation to ensure ethical use and accurate interpretation of AI-derived indicators.
- Sustainability risks without long-term funding, governance structures, and technical maintenance capacity.
governance_measures: Data protection / confidentiality procedures;Human-in-the-loop oversight;Documentation of model and limitations
ethics_note: The system incorporates human-in-the-loop validation, transparent indicator formulas, and documented assumptions to ensure accountable and ethical use of AI-derived outputs. Special attention is given to the representation of vulnerable groups through the integration of census and administrative data, including gender and protection indicators. Data governance protocols, role-based access controls, and ethical data-sharing agreements are applied to protect sensitive information. The system is designed to support decision-making rather than replace it, with final actions determined through established government coordination and accountability mechanisms.

business_need: The business need or problem being addressed through this chatbot initiative at Mongolia's National Statistical Office (NSO) is the difficulty in providing fast, accurate, accessible, and efficient responses to a high volume of user queries about official statistics, while reducing the manual workload on NSO staff and improving overall data dissemination.
description: The National Statistical Office of Mongolia (NSO) has introduced an NLP-based AI chatbot to address the need for providing users with fast and accurate responses to their questions. This chatbot automatically processes queries on the website (for example: "What is the GDP growth rate for 2025?") and directly retrieves and delivers answers from official data sources. As a result, user satisfaction has increased, while the workload on staff has decreased.
benefits:
The National Statistical Office of Mongolia (NSO) has introduced MonStatGPT, and the main benefits observed can be summarized as follows:
- Significantly reduced response times and user query burden
- Improved user satisfaction and accessibility
- Enhanced timeliness and efficiency of data dissemination
- Cost savings and resource efficiency
challenges:
- Large language models (LLMs) used in the chatbot have relatively limited Mongolian-language official statistical content in their training data, making it difficult to accurately understand and process specialized terminology and numerical indicators.
- Although the model operates in Mongolian, there is a high risk of errors when handling queries involving precise professional terms.
- Additionally, the AI model sometimes provides incorrect information regarding detailed statistical calculations.
- The NSO faces a shortage of specialists to maintain, update, and monitor the AI model, including addressing model drift over time.
governance_measures: Documentation of model and limitations;Data protection / confidentiality procedures
ethics_note:
This chatbot initiative incorporates careful consideration of ethics, bias, and accountability:
- Ethics: The chatbot retrieves and delivers information exclusively from the verified official source (1212.mn database of the National Statistical Office), ensuring accuracy, impartiality, and integrity of official statistics. No personal user data is collected or stored, and privacy protection principles are strictly followed.
- Bias: Large language models have relatively limited Mongolian-language official statistical content in their training data, which may lead to linguistic or contextual bias.
- Accountability: NSO staff monitor and validate AI-generated responses, especially for complex or critical queries.

title: Ananda (Asisten Neraca Anda): Multimodal AI Assistant for National Accounts Document Retrieval
gsbpm_phases: Build -  Develop and test tools, systems, and workflows for production;Analyse - Produce, interpret, validate, and finalize statistical outputs;Disseminate - Release and promote statistical products and support users;Evaluate -  Review the process and outputs to identify improvements
purpose: Text extraction / summarisation: Extracting structured information from text or generating summaries of longer documents;Chatbots / virtual assistants: Providing automated responses or guidance to users through conversational interfaces;Dissemination / communication: Supporting the presentation, explanation, or communication of statistics (e.g. generating statistical releases, narratives, data visualisations, metadata, or user-facing summaries)
tools_used: Uses open-source tools;Uses commercial free tools;Uses commercial paid tools
maturity: Pilot (limited use): The AI application has been tested using real data in a controlled or limited operational setting, but is not yet part of regular production processes
business_need: System of National Accounts documentation contains detailed methodological guidance that is essential for economic statistics compilation, but locating specific information within multiple documents can be time-consuming. This creates challenges for both internal users and statistical staff who need quick and reliable access to definitions, concepts, and accounting rules. The initiative addresses this need by developing an AI-assisted retrieval and question answering tool to support more efficient use of statistical documentation.
description: AI is used through a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach, where users submit natural language questions through a web chat interface and the system retrieves relevant content from System of National Accounts documents. A language model then generates responses grounded in the retrieved material. In addition, a self-reflective mechanism is applied to assess whether the retrieved information is sufficient and relevant before producing the final answer, helping improve response quality and consistency.
benefits: Initial evaluation shows promising results in response quality and relevance. The prototype achieved 86% answer correctness and 95% answer relevancy, indicating strong performance in generating responses aligned with user queries. Retrieval evaluation also showed 92% text context relevancy, suggesting that relevant textual evidence is generally identified effectively. Lower scores were observed for multimodal grounding, with image context relevancy at 69%, text faithfulness at 69%, and image faithfulness at 64%, highlighting areas for further improvement in grounding and multimodal response consistency.
challenges: The main challenges encountered relate to ensuring consistent grounding of responses across multimodal statistical documents, particularly when combining textual and visual information. While text retrieval performs well, image-based context remains more difficult to interpret reliably, which affects faithfulness in some responses. Additional challenges include the technical complexity of domain-specific statistical terminology in System of National Accounts documentation and the need to balance response quality with retrieval precision in a prototype environment.
governance_measures: Human-in-the-loop oversight;Documentation of model and limitations
ethics_note: The system is intended to support, not replace, expert interpretation of official statistical documents. Responses remain grounded in retrieved source material, and human review is important for technical use cases. Known limitations are documented, particularly for multimodal responses.
links:
Public source code related to the self-reflective retrieval mechanism is available via GitHub: https://github.com/faarh-nn/self-multimodal-rag.git

Additional technical documentation, including a technical paper, presentation materials, and user interface component is available upon request.

business_need: Business surveys collect free-text descriptions of economic activities, which must be mapped to standardized industrial classification systems such as PSIC. Manual coding is resource-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to inconsistencies due to subjective interpretation. With large volumes of records, there was a need for a scalable and consistent approach to automate classification while maintaining accuracy and alignment with statistical standards. The initiative aims to reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and accelerate processing of business data used in official statistics.
description: The initiative follows a hybrid approach combining manual expertise and AI techniques. Initially, a sample of 10,000 records was manually coded and validated through ground verification. Keywords and activity patterns were extracted to build rule-based matching logic. A Random Forest classifier was then trained on labeled data to automate classification of business descriptions. Subsequently, a Large Language Model (LLM) was trained on cleaned and codified data to enhance classification performance on more complex or ambiguous descriptions. Outputs from AI models are cross-validated and subjected to final ground verification, ensuring reliability and consistency in assigned classification codes.
benefits: The approach significantly reduces manual coding effort and improves consistency in classification. It enables faster processing of large datasets and provides scalable support for business surveys. The combination of rule-based methods and machine learning improves accuracy, while LLM integration enhances handling of complex and unstructured descriptions. Overall, the system contributes to more efficient and standardized statistical production processes.
challenges: Challenges include variability and ambiguity in business descriptions, limited labeled training data, and maintaining classification accuracy across diverse economic activities. Ensuring model explainability and alignment with official classification standards is critical. Integration of multiple approaches (rules, ML, LLM) requires careful validation. Human oversight remains necessary to handle edge cases and ensure quality, particularly where descriptions are incomplete or unclear.
governance_measures: Data protection / confidentiality procedures;Human-in-the-loop oversight;Documentation of model and limitations
ethics_note: Human validation is maintained to ensure transparency and accountability in classification decisions. Potential bias is monitored, particularly in cases of ambiguous or incomplete descriptions.

business_need: The eSankhyiki platform hosts a large repository of statistical publications, datasets, and reports produced by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the MoSPI. However, users often face challenges in locating relevant information using traditional keyword-based search mechanisms. Statistical documents are typically lengthy and contain complex terminology, making it difficult for users to quickly find specific indicators, tables, or contextual insights. The primary business need was to improve discoverability, accessibility, and usability of statistical information available on the eSankhyiki platform.
description: The initiative uses Artificial Intelligence, specifically Natural Language Processing (NLP) and transformer-based semantic search models, to enhance the search functionality of the eSankhyiki platform. Instead of relying on traditional keyword matching, the system converts both user queries and statistical content into vector embeddings using pre-trained language models and  provides best possible matches in terms of datasets.
benefits:
Improved search accuracy and relevance, Reduced time required to find relevant data and reports, 
Enhanced usability of statistical repositories, Improved accessibility of statistical knowledge.
challenges: Key challenges include domain embedding mismatch, where general language models may not fully capture statistical terminology used in official datasets. Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search errors may occasionally affect retrieval accuracy when identifying the most relevant semantic matches. Query intent ambiguity can also lead to multiple possible interpretations of user queries. Additionally, optimizing hybrid ranking mechanisms that combine semantic similarity with metadata filters remains complex. Extracting structured filters (e.g., year, sector, state) from natural language queries also presents challenges in ensuring accurate and consistent search results.

Traditional keyword-based search methods require users to know the exact terminology, making the process time-consuming and error-prone. The initiative aims to simplify the identification of appropriate NIC codes by enabling an intelligent search mechanism that allows users to retrieve relevant classifications based on the meaning and context of their queries.
description: The solution uses Artificial Intelligence techniques such as Natural Language Processing (NLP) and transformer-based semantic search models to improve NIC code discovery. description: The Intelligent Document Search system uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) and transformer-based language models to perform semantic search across document repositories. The most semantically relevant sections or documents are then retrieved and ranked, allowing users to locate relevant information quickly without relying on exact keyword matches.
benefits: Faster retrieval of relevant document content, Reduced manual effort in searching through large documents, Improved access to institutional knowledge, Enhanced productivity for analysts and policymakers
challenges: Key challenges include handling unstructured document formats, ensuring consistent document indexing, maintaining accuracy across diverse document types, and ensuring explainability of AI-generated search results.

maturity: Production (operational): The AI application is integrated into routine statistical operations and is used on a regular basis to support official statistics
business_need: Enterprise owners, bookkeepers (or the public in general), have ability to contact to the NSI to get the guidance regarding NACE rev.2 codes and get the advice on what would be the suitable code for given economic activity. The contact usually takes place via a phone call, and it requires in-person involvement of SBR division employees.
description: Using the online chat-bot, users can get the guidance/advice regarding the NACE rev.2 codes of described economic activity without a direct, in-person involvement of the NSI team. The process is similar to the phone call as the users can describe the economic activity in natural terms, if the destabilization is insufficient, the chat-bot asks for additional details and guides the user on what information to include. The chat-bot gives either the definite answer (when the description given by the user is proper/exact enough to match only one code of NACE classification), or the list of potential codes as an output.
benefits: There are limited number of employees at the SBR division and, although this does not happen in practice, there is a chance that more users will contact the NSI at the same time than the team can handle. In times like this, the chat-bot is advantageous as it can handle virtually unlimited requests simultaneously. More importantly, the NACE chat-bot eases the workload of the SBR employees and provides additional mean of communication with the users who do not (want to) use the phone-call feature.
challenges: Chat-bot service is provided to the general public free-of-charge, but the NSI pays for the underling software service. Subsequently, if the demand on the service exceeds the NSI expectations, this might lead to overspending. Also, despite the chat-bot asks clarifying questions to the user, there is still a chance of miscommunication and the chat-bot showing incorrect NACE rev.2 code output to the users. That is why the chat-bot webpage reads "The 100% accuracy of the NACE Rev.2 activity code suggested by the system is not guaranteed. It is advisable to verify the result in the national classifier."
governance_measures: No specific measures beyond usual practice
links: Bilingual (Georgian and English) portal for the NACE rev.2 code chat-bot is available at https://nace.geostat.ge/

title: AI-Powered Automated Receipt Parsing for the Household Expenditure Survey (HES)
lead_organisation: Census and Statistics Department (C&SD), Hong Kong SAR
statistical_domains: Population and social statistics;Internal operations / workflow
gsbpm_phases: Process - Clean, integrate, classify, validate, and transform data
purpose: Text extraction / summarisation: Extracting structured information from text or generating summaries of longer documents;Workflow optimisation / internal support: Automating or improving internal processes (e.g. task routing, document handling, code assistance)
maturity: Pilot (limited use): The AI application has been tested using real data in a controlled or limited operational setting, but is not yet part of regular production processes
business_need: For the Household Expenditure Survey (HES), C&SD processes massive volumes of consumer receipts uploaded by households to analyse local spending patterns. These receipts originate from diverse sources (supermarkets, restaurants, e-commerce) in varying formats, often mixing Chinese and English text. Traditionally, staff had to manually identify and input fields such as merchant name, purchase date, item descriptions, quantities, and prices. This manual data entry process is highly repetitive, time-consuming, and susceptible to human error.
description: C&SD deployed a Vision-Language Model (Qwen2.5-VL) on its internal Big Data Analytics Platform (BDAP) to automate receipt parsing. The AI pipeline ingests receipt images (JPG/PNG/PDF) and uses a defined prompt schema to extract target variables automatically. The system handles exceptions through a retry mechanism and outputs structured JSON or Excel files. Staff focus is shifted from manual transcription to sample-based human verification, transforming a labour-intensive workflow into an automated, rule-based process.
benefits: The automated pipeline is projected to reduce overall receipt processing time by approximately 90% (from 360 workdays down to just 12 days) upon full implementation, achieving a 30-fold efficiency gain. Additionally, it significantly reduces human transcription errors. The structured JSON/Excel outputs preserve data lineage, ensuring the process is fully traceable and easier to audit during the sampling and verification stages.
challenges: The system must navigate unstructured inputs, blurry images, and varied receipt formats. To address output truncations, a 'continuation' mechanism was built to stitch together split responses. A dedicated error-handling protocol skips and logs invalid files for targeted retries, ensuring the batch-processing workflow remains uninterrupted.
ethics_note: The model is hosted entirely on C&SD's on-premise BDAP infrastructure, ensuring that sensitive respondent microdata never leaves the department's secure environment.

title: AI in processing trade documents – Anomaly Detection
lead_organisation: Census and Statistics Department (C&SD), Hong Kong SAR
gsbpm_phases: Process - Clean, integrate, classify, validate, and transform data;Analyse - Produce, interpret, validate, and finalize statistical outputs
models_or_algorithms: Predictive models and NLP algorithms (for tokenisation, stemming, string similarity scoring)
purpose: Anomaly detection / quality assurance: Identifying unusual patterns, outliers, or potential quality issues in data or processes;Record linkage / matching: Linking records relating to the same entity across different datasets or sources.;Workflow optimisation / internal support: Automating or improving internal processes (e.g. task routing, document handling, code assistance)
maturity: Production (operational): The AI application is integrated into routine statistical operations and is used on a regular basis to support official statistics
business_need: C&SD processes approximately 70,000 import/export trade declarations daily to compile external merchandise trade statistics. Traditionally, verifying millions of commodity classifications and declared unit values against cargo manifests required extensive manual review of unstructured, free-text goods descriptions. Conventional rule-based systems were limited to exact matching only (e.g., exact Bill of Lading numbers), causing a massive backlog of manual checks and inefficiencies in identifying non-lodged declarations.
description: Since 2018, C&SD has developed in-house AI models using deep learning algorithms trained on millions of labelled commodity descriptions. The system leverages Natural Language Processing (NLP) to normalise unstructured text (via tokenisation and stemming) and calculates string similarity scores (fuzzy partial ratio) to compare goods descriptions between trade declarations and manifests. Additionally, the AI mimics human decision-making by applying fault-tolerance for common typos (e.g., confusing "O" and "0") and uses a risk-based approach to filter out low-risk manifests.
benefits: By early 2024, the AI integration achieved a remarkable 40% reduction in manpower for manual checking procedures. It ensured operational resilience during pandemic-related manpower constraints. The massive efficiency gains allowed C&SD to restructure and redistribute human resources to establish new strategic branches focused on data science and digital transformation.
challenges: Developing trust in the AI required an "incremental approach" and stringent quality assurance. C&SD managed the transition by rolling out models in stages (Air, Water, and then Road transport modes) to reduce operational impact.
ethics_note: The model ensures accountability through a collaborative framework where the user section  continuously provides feedback on model results to the R&D section to refine the algorithms and minimise systemic bias.

title: 2026 Census Auto-coding of industry and occupation
lead_organisation: Census and Statistics Department (C&SD), Hong Kong SAR
statistical_domains: Population and social statistics;Internal operations / workflow
gsbpm_phases: Process - Clean, integrate, classify, validate, and transform data
purpose: Classification / coding: Assigning records to categories or codes (e.g. industry, occupation, product, topic).;Workflow optimisation / internal support: Automating or improving internal processes (e.g. task routing, document handling, code assistance)
maturity: Production (operational): The AI application is integrated into routine statistical operations and is used on a regular basis to support official statistics
business_need: During previous Censuses, coding the free-text responses for open-ended industry and occupation questions was a fully manual process. Staff had to manually read these multilingual descriptions and assign the corresponding numerical classification codes (e.g., 3-digit industry codes and 2- or 4-digit occupation codes). This manual coding process was highly resource-intensive and time-consuming for large-scale statistical exercises.
description: C&SD developed an AI Classification Model using a pre-trained multilingual Large Language Model (mBERT) based on Transformer architecture. The model was fine-tuned using around 328k records from the 2021 Census and GHS data. It takes multilingual free-text responses from questionnaires, tokenises them, and predicts the occupation and industry codes alongside a probability score. The framework operates via an API within the Departmental Data Collection Platform and incorporates a risk-based, human-in-the-loop mechanism.
benefits: The auto-coding application has significantly reduced manual coding efforts. Through the risk-based mechanism and human-in-the-loop application, the overall classification accuracy is extremely high, achieving 97.0% for Occupation Codes and 95.1% for Industry Codes. Furthermore, the system is highly extendable; its API-based architecture allows other surveys to adopt the same models easily and configure sampling rules based on their specific needs.
challenges: To mitigate the risk of inaccurate AI predictions, C&SD implemented a robust human-in-the-loop sampling mechanism. Predictions with low confidence probabilities, as well as results falling into classes with historically low accuracy, are automatically flagged and sampled for manual coding. Additionally, some high-confidence outputs are sampled to continuously monitor and ensure the quality of the model's performance.
governance_measures: Data protection / confidentiality procedures;Human-in-the-loop oversight;Data minimization, processed entirely on internal servers
ethics_note: Accountability is maintained through a built-in confidence threshold where low-probability results default back to human coders, ensuring the AI assists rather than overrides human judgment.
